children: SYDNEY--Challenger shares hit their highest level since 2018 after the Australian investment manager said it was considering a takeover bid from Daiichi Life Group.
ASX-listed Challenger said the Japanese insurer's approach valued its equity at 7.97 billion Australian dollars, equivalent to US$5.54 billion.
Daiichi Life, Challenger's largest shareholder with a stake of nearly 21%, has offered A$11.80 a share for all the stock that it doesn't already own.
Challenger shares were up 18% at A$11.58 in early trade. They haven't closed above that level since August 2018.
The offer price represents a roughly 20% premium to Challenger's Friday closing share price of A$9.85.
In a separate announcement, Challenger said its assets under management rose 5% over the September quarter to A$31.9 billion.
